findings.note: Recovery treats a target whose current hash equals PRE as safely restored and may delete the journal at line 2151 without re-establishing durability for that target's parent directory. If an earlier rollback replacement or ABSENT-state unlink succeeded but its parent-directory fsync failed, the journal is correctly retained while the live view already appears PRE; on the next invocation this branch accepts that volatile PRE state, and the round-29 barrier fsyncs only resolver-evidence.yaml's parent. In a Full transaction the Context Projection has a different parent, so journal deletion can become durable while a later crash loses the unconfirmed rollback and resurrects its POST entry, leaving a published artifact with no recovery journal. This is outside ruling (c) because it requires no attacker-authored journal, and the bundle's mutation capture explicitly leaves the related unlink-side durability mutant O uncovered.
